title: Email Header Analysis: ProtonMail Anomaly

fields.subject: Something will happen at NCIA at exactly 12:00 PM today. You won't find it in time. But you're welcome to try.

headers.name: From
headers.note: ProtonMail-encrypted sender; no real identity visible

headers.name: Subject
headers.value: Something will happen at NCIA at exactly 12:00 PM today. You won't find it in time. But you're welcome to try.
headers.note: Contains time-specific threat; matches exercise timeline

headers.name: Date
headers.note: Timezone header: UTC-5 (Eastern Time); matches local airport clock

headers.name: User-Agent
headers.value: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/122.0.6261.112 Safari/537.36
headers.note: Indicates Windows 11 OS and Chrome 122; consistent with contractor's known environment

headers.name: Received
headers.note: Internal hop from AODB server (10.66.0.10) — likely a system mailbox

headers.name: Received
headers.note: Second hop from badging workstation (10.66.0.50) — suggests spoofed or compromised local system

fields.conclusion: This email is a high-priority threat indicator. It was sent from a ProtonMail account using end-to-end encryption and routed through Swiss servers via Tor, rendering standard IP tracing ineffective. The sender used a Windows 11 environment with Chrome 122 and explicitly set the timezone to UTC-5, aligning with local airport time. The message contains a time-bound threat targeting 12:00 PM today, which matches the exercise timeline. The email passed through NCIA-PACS-CORE (10.66.0.10) and NCIA-ENROLL (10.66.0.50), both critical assets in the SecNet. While no authentication checks pass, the user-agent and timezone metadata may provide indirect linkage to the former contractor, Dmitri Volkov, if cross-referenced with offboarding logs. No direct evidence of compromise found yet, but the sender's behavior suggests deliberate obfuscation. Treat as a red herring for now, but preserve all headers for later correlation.

instructorNote: This inject tests if the team spends time chasing dead-end forensic leads. The Windows 11/Chrome 122/UTC-5 metadata will be useful later if they follow up on A-20. Do not let them waste time on ProtonMail tracing.

citations.quote: All USB ports on the Badging Workstation and Core Servers are physically disabled or blocked via GPO. *End of Document*
